thinkingMap.title: A tool library for the street
thinkingMap.seedIdea: Four people on my street have each bought a tile cutter they used once. I want to fix that, but every version of it I imagine collapses the moment someone moves away.

message.content: Four people on my street have each bought a tile cutter they used once. I want to fix that, but every version of it I imagine collapses the moment someone moves away.
The collapsing is the interesting part. Before we design the lending: who is it for, what happens when something comes back broken, and where do the tools actually live?

mapNode.label: A tool library for the street
mapNode.detail: Nobody on this street needs to own a tile cutter, and four of us have bought one.

mapNode.label: Who is this for — you, or the whole street?
mapNode.options: ["Just my building", "The whole street", "Anyone who can walk here"]

mapNode.label: What happens when something comes back broken?
mapNode.options: ["The borrower replaces it", "A shared repair fund", "We just accept the loss"]

mapNode.label: Where would the tools physically live?
mapNode.options: ["Somebody's garage", "The building's bike room", "A rented locker"]

mapNode.label: It has to survive me going away for a month
mapNode.detail: Contributed directly: if the whole thing stops working the moment one person is unavailable, it is not a library, it is a favour.

mapNode.label: Every tool library that lasted had two keyholders
mapNode.detail: Across the four write-ups I could find, the ones that folded had a single custodian and the ones still running had at least two.

mapNode.label: Who is the second person holding a key?
mapNode.options: ["Someone already named", "Nobody yet", "I would rather it be a lockbox"]

mapNode.label: Does anyone pay anything, ever?
mapNode.options: ["Free, always", "A yearly membership", "Pay only when you break something"]
